_help: VPN providers for stark-vpn and the HUD (Control Center tile, bar, Settings → NETWORK).
Fields: id (used by `stark-vpn toggle <id>` and `qs ipc call vpn toggle <id>`), name (short, shown on the tile),
label (longer, shown in Settings), type (protonvpn | nm), enabled.
Only one provider is connected at a time; connecting one disconnects the others.

providers.name: PROTON
providers.label: Proton VPN (free)
providers._country: empty = fastest free server anywhere; or a code like CA / NL / US

providers.name: SCHOOL
providers.label: School (Cisco)
_setup: Cisco Secure Client / AnyConnect VPNs work with openconnect through NetworkManager, no Cisco client needed:
1. sudo pacman -S networkmanager-openconnect   (then: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager)
2. nmcli con add type vpn vpn-type openconnect con-name School vpn.data 'gateway=vpn.<university>.edu,protocol=anyconnect'
(add usergroup=<group> to vpn.data if the school uses one; KDE System Settings → Connections → + → Cisco AnyConnect works too)
3. Connect once by hand (nmcli --ask con up id School) so NM saves what it can; SSO / MFA logins open the openconnect auth dialog,
which needs a running NM secret agent (KDE's plasma-nm, or nm-applet) — otherwise the HUD connect fails with 'no secrets'.
4. Here: set "connection": "School" and "enabled": true. The HUD picks it up on its own.
